wire.remote_compute.api_override.role: CLI warning printed to STDERR when the remote-compute API base is overridden
wire.remote_compute.api_override.tone: plain, two sentences; the variable name and the host stay verbatim; it states the consequence rather than only the fact
wire.remote_compute.api_override.note: {host} is the exact host and port the bearer is being sent to, WITHOUT any credential and without a path — it is the whole point of the line and must be preserved exactly once. Printed once per invocation, to stderr, before the first request, so stdout stays the run id alone, and on --remote-status and --remote-cancel as well. The second sentence is the operative fact: the Radient LOGIN leaves for that host, and the variable should be unset unless the reader controls it. A login going to a staging server must never look like one going to production, and the reader must be able to act on the sentence without knowing what a bearer is.

wire.remote_compute.api_override_invalid.note: No placeholders. The value itself is never echoed. The character rules are one of them refused by the parser before it splits the value, so they belong in the same sentence rather than a second one.
